### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via cloudManaged (symbol, a field of const object PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5d2149f9fa2dae4dfe3a2acd91f98927118d75b9` — the merge of head `3e0188a72d7d3258a40489bc0aa36cfa3344d515` into base `bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5d2149f9fa2dae4dfe3a2acd91f98927118d75b9 && git checkout 5d2149f9fa2dae4dfe3a2acd91f98927118d75b9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262 3e0188a72d7d3258a40489bc0aa36cfa3344d515 && git checkout -B drift-repro bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262 && git merge --no-ff 3e0188a72d7d3258a40489bc0aa36cfa3344d515

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8883bc6e553de0150f8d3850926e6a253730af00`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-invitation.object.ts

Inputs read: card #33758 (body, the Claim 6895913757, the os-dev-report 6896465232; no ruling and no earlier record on the card), PR #33956 (body, 5 files, net diff against `main` at merge-base `895783a1`), and the check-runs on the head. The remainder of the diff (`cloud-managed-visibility.test.ts`, `platform-objects.test.ts`, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` and is not judged in ④; the two test files were read only as the enforcement of the booking.

Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-11-15T15:01Z: 20 `success`, 11 `skipped`, 0 failed, 32 still `in_progress`. Concluded green: `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`. Not yet concluded: `Test Core (1/8 to 8/8)`, `Test UI (1/16 to 16/16)`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check UI`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`. The test shards that hold this change's pins (`feature-gate-guard.test.ts`, `platform-objects.test.ts`, `cloud-managed-visibility.test.ts`) are among the unconcluded ones, so this record does not report them green; nothing was run locally in their place. The verdict below is the design judgment on this head; a red on any of those runs is the merge queue's refusal and is not covered by it.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged. No zod schema, no authorable key, no accepted value moves. `PublicAuthFeatureEntry`, `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURE_NAMES` and `featureGatePredicate` are untouched; `requiresFeature` still names the same closed flag set. Right.
- Public surface: `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.cloudManaged.gatedInputs` gains one string, `sys_invitation.actions.resend_invitation`. The export set of `@objectstack/spec/kernel` is the same (`api-surface/kernel.json` and `export-origins/kernel.json` list names, and neither is in the diff). The const's literal tuple type grows by one member; no consumer in the tree indexes that tuple by position (the only reader of `gatedInputs` is `feature-gate-guard.test.ts`, which iterates). Right.
- Served metadata: `sys_invitation.resend_invitation`'s lowered `visible` goes from `INVITE && ORG` to `((features.cloudManaged != true) && INVITE) && ORG`, the shape of the `invite_user` row beside it. This narrows where a platform action is offered on one deployment mode; it is not something a metadata author writes. Right.
- Served `/auth/config`: unchanged; the flag was already served and classified. Right.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/platform-objects` and `@objectstack/spec`, with `Metadata-protocol: none`: correct. Both packages publish a changed file, no authorable key or accepted value moves (kind `none` takes `patch`), and `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on the head.

Clause-②: no. The plain arm is the right one: `(narrowing)` is the BREAKING arm for a declared capability taken away at the consumer, and nothing is taken away here. The door `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/invite-member` already refuses every call on a cloud-managed environment (below), so the action removed from the row is one that could only answer `409`. The PR body and the changeset body both carry the line, and `PR-body guards` concluded `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the os-dev-report. Nothing to answer.
- `out_of_scope_findings`, one entry (carrier: none): `resend_invitation` carries no `status` term of its own, the rows it appears on being decided by the list views that project it. Answered: true on `main` before this PR and unchanged by it, and the card asks for the managed gate only. Not a defect of this diff; no card owed by this record.
- `security_findings`: none. Agreed: `visible` is courtesy, and the enforcement is the server refusal, which this diff does not touch.
- Forced test edit (`platform-objects.test.ts`, the `resend_invitation` lowering row): legitimate. The row pins the served predicate byte for byte, so it must move with the gate, and it moves to the same shape as the `invite_user` row above it.
- Two NOT-MEASURED gate families in the dev's local reconciliation (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`): neither reads a file this diff touches; both belong to CI runs, of which `Lint · repo & tooling gates` is green and `Build Core` is unconcluded (see above).

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts` (hits). The booking is held against the contract the file states for `gatedInputs` and against its one consumer, `packages/platform-objects/src/feature-gate-guard.test.ts`:

- Path grammar: `sys_invitation.actions.resend_invitation` matches the action form, and the action exists on the object under that name.
- Forward row: the guard requires the target's lowered `visible` to carry `featureGatePredicate('cloudManaged')`, which is `features.cloudManaged != true` for a `hide-when-on` flag, as one `&&` conjunct. The authored `visible` is exactly that string, and the lowered form `((gate) && INVITE) && ORG` is the fourth positive case of the guard's own matcher table. Holds.
- Reverse row: every `features.*` reference in a `visible` must be booked under its flag. Without this line the new term would be unbooked; with it, both references on the action (`cloudManaged`, `organization`) are booked, `organization` already at line 148. Holds, and the booking is necessary, not decorative.
- The entry's `notes` sentence, "Each gated input is also gated on `organization` or `admin`, so its `visible` predicate carries two gates", stays true: this input carries `organization`.
- `SHOWN_WHEN_ON` is not touched and must not be: this input is hidden while the flag is on, the one polarity the registry models.
- The inline comment, "A resend is a call to invite-member, which refuses it here", was checked against the code it cites. `auth-manager-before-hook.ts` (on `main`, around L751 to L770) throws `APIError('CONFLICT')` with `CLOUD_MANAGED_REFUSAL_CODE` for `ctx.path === '/organization/invite-member' && isCloudManaged()`, a path-only match placed ahead of the vendor handler precisely because better-auth answers `resend: true` before it consults `beforeCreateInvitation`. The comment there names this very action as the console's route into that branch. The claim holds.
- Placement between the four mirrors and `copy_invitation_link` leaves the mirrors' comment block describing four entries, and the new line has its own comment. The `organization` block's neighbouring comment, "same gates as resend", is still accurate.

`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-invitation.object.ts` (implementing). Read sentence by sentence against the contract:

- `visible: 'features.cloudManaged != true'` is byte-identical to the term on `sys_invitation.invite_user` (L88) and to the leading conjunct of `copy_invitation_link`, so the three admin-side invitation doors of the object now agree; `cancel_invitation` stays offered, which is right, since cancelling a pending row is not an invite-member call and is not refused.
- Fault direction: an action's `visible` is fail-soft, so a console holding no `cloudManaged` key keeps Resend shown, the same answer as the flag being off and the same as its siblings. No new way to hide the action off a managed environment.
- The comment's two claims, that the mirrors and `copy_invitation_link` are hidden the same way and that the refusal is in `auth-manager-before-hook.ts` with resends included, are both true in the tree.
- Attempts to break it: (a) a second door for a resend that is not refused, so that hiding the button would remove something that works: none, `auth-route-ledger.ts` has `organizations.invite` and `organizations.invitations.resend` both target the one refused route; (b) the gate landing under a disjunction after lowering, where it would gate nothing: no, the lowering row pins it as a top-level conjunct group; (c) the action being offered on a row where Resend is the only remedy on a managed environment: no, an expired pending row's resend is the same refused call.

No must-fix, no should-fix. No nit.
